content.value_statement: Medical device teams need clear FDA, QSR, HIPAA, and cybersecurity planning. This skill structures regulatory strategy, submission preparation, and compliance reviews.
actual_capabilities: Explains FDA pathway selection across 510(k), PMA, De Novo, and pre-submission planning.
Outlines QSR 21 CFR 820 controls, including design controls, document controls, and CAPA.
Frames HIPAA safeguards and PHI risk assessment topics for connected medical devices.
Summarizes SaMD, combination product, cybersecurity, inspection readiness, and warning letter response considerations.
Lists intended FDA, QSR, HIPAA, cybersecurity, and inspection resource areas for planning.
limitations: Does not replace legal, clinical, quality, or regulatory counsel.
Includes placeholder script, reference, and asset files rather than working FDA tools.
Does not verify current FDA guidance or submission status without user-provided sources.
Cannot guarantee FDA clearance, approval, or inspection outcomes.

use_cases.title: Select an FDA Pathway
use_cases.description: Compare 510(k), PMA, De Novo, and pre-submission considerations for an early device strategy discussion.

use_cases.title: Prepare a QSR Gap Review
use_cases.description: Organize design controls, document controls, management responsibility, and CAPA topics before an internal quality review.

use_cases.title: Assess Connected Device Compliance
use_cases.description: Review HIPAA safeguards, PHI data flows, cybersecurity controls, and FDA software documentation needs.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Pathway Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review for a device concept.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain whether my medical device may fit 510(k), PMA, or De Novo. Ask for device type, intended use, predicate candidates, risks, and software details first.

prompt_templates.title: Build a QSR Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a QSR 21 CFR 820 readiness checklist for our device team. Cover design controls, document controls, management responsibility, CAPA, and evidence needed.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Pre-Submission Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Help plan an FDA Q-Sub strategy for this device. Identify key questions, missing evidence, testing topics, timeline risks, and assumptions to validate.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Regulatory and Security Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an integrated plan for FDA pathway, QSR documentation, HIPAA safeguards, cybersecurity evidence, inspection readiness, and launch decision points.

output_examples.input: I am preparing a 510(k) for a connected wearable that stores patient data.
output: Likely review areas include predicate comparison, intended use, performance testing, software validation, cybersecurity controls, and HIPAA safeguard documentation.
Open assumptions include device classification, clinical claims, PHI data flow, wireless connectivity risks, and whether FDA pre-submission feedback is needed.

output_examples.input: Our team needs a QSR gap review before an internal audit.
output: Start with design controls, document controls, management responsibility, and CAPA records.
For each area, map procedures, objective evidence, owner, current gap, corrective action, and review date.

output_examples.input: We received FDA questions about software changes and cybersecurity.
output_examples.output: The response plan should map each FDA question to evidence, clarify software impact, document cybersecurity risk controls, and identify any testing updates.

best_practices: Provide device classification, intended use, predicate candidates, risk profile, and software details at the start.
Ask the model to separate regulatory assumptions from confirmed facts.
Validate outputs against current FDA guidance and qualified professional review before use.
anti_patterns: Do not submit generated text to FDA without expert review and source verification.
Do not provide PHI or confidential patient data unless your environment permits it.
Do not ask the skill to guarantee clearance, approval, or compliance outcomes.

faq.question: Can this skill replace an FDA consultant?
faq.answer: No. It helps organize regulatory thinking, but qualified professional review is still required.

faq.question: Does it create complete FDA submissions?
faq.answer: It can help structure submission content and evidence needs. Complete submissions require device-specific data, testing, and review.

faq.question: Can it evaluate HIPAA obligations?
faq.answer: It can organize HIPAA safeguard topics and risk assessment questions. It does not provide a legal determination.

faq.question: Does the included script perform FDA tracking?
faq.answer: No. The packaged script is a placeholder and does not implement FDA tracking.

faq.question: Can it help with SaMD planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It can frame SaMD classification, software documentation, cybersecurity, and change control topics.

faq.question: Which AI tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
